ucs.title: [LLM] Gamaredon Telegraph/Telegram dead-drop resolver C2 retrieval
ucs.description: Detects Gamaredon (Shuckworm / Aqua Blizzard / Primitive Bear) implants such as Pterodo, GammaLoad, GammaSteel, and PteroPSLoad fetching their next-stage C2 address from Telegraph (telegra.ph / graph.org), Telegram (t.me), or IPFS pages used as dead-drop resolvers. The actor publishes hex/base64-encoded IPs in public posts so implants can rotate infrastructure without re-deployment — non-browser/non-Telegram-client processes calling these domains is highly anomalous.
ucs.splunk:
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) AS firstTime max(_time) AS lastTime FROM datamodel=Network_Resolution WHERE (DNS.query="*telegra.ph" OR DNS.query="*te.legra.ph" OR DNS.query="*graph.org" OR DNS.query="*t.me" OR DNS.query="*telegram.org" OR DNS.query="*ipfs.io" OR DNS.query="*cloudflare-ipfs.com") BY DNS.src DNS.query host _time span=5m
| `drop_dm_object_name(DNS)`
| rename src AS dest
| join type=inner dest [
    | tstats `summariesonly` count FROM datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
        WHERE (Processes.process_name IN ("mshta.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","bitsadmin.exe","hh.exe","cmd.exe")
            OR Processes.process_path IN ("*\\Users\\Public\\*","*\\AppData\\Local\\Temp\\*","*\\AppData\\Roaming\\Microsoft\\*","*\\ProgramData\\*"))
        AND NOT (Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","telegram.exe","TelegramDesktop.exe","Teams.exe","slack.exe","opera.exe"))
        AND NOT (Processes.user="*$")
        BY Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.process_name Processes.process Processes.parent_process_name
    | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`]
| `security_content_ctime(firstTime)`
| `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
| table firstTime lastTime dest user process_name parent_process_name process query count
ucs.kql:
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let DeadDropDomains = dynamic(["telegra.ph","te.legra.ph","graph.org","t.me","telegram.org","ipfs.io","cloudflare-ipfs.com"]);
let LegitClients = dynamic(["chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","iexplore.exe","opera.exe","telegram.exe","telegramdesktop.exe","slack.exe","teams.exe","discord.exe"]);
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where isnotempty(RemoteUrl)
| where RemoteUrl has_any (DeadDropDomains)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ (LegitClients)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("mshta.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","bitsadmin.exe","hh.exe","cmd.exe")
   or InitiatingProcessFolderPath has_any (@"\Users\Public\", @"\AppData\Local\Temp\", @"\AppData\Roaming\Microsoft\", @"\ProgramData\")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName,
          AccountName = InitiatingProcessAccountName,
          Process = InitiatingProcessFileName,
          ProcessPath = InitiatingProcessFolderPath,
          Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          Parent = InitiatingProcessParentFileName,
          RemoteUrl, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| order by Timestamp desc
ucs.sentinel_kql:
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let DeadDropDomains = dynamic(["telegra.ph","te.legra.ph","graph.org","t.me","telegram.org","ipfs.io","cloudflare-ipfs.com"]);
let SuspectClients = dynamic(["mshta.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","bitsadmin.exe","hh.exe","cmd.exe"]);
let dnshits = DnsEvents
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where QueryType in ("A","AAAA")
    | where Name has_any (DeadDropDomains)
    | project DnsTime = TimeGenerated, Computer, ClientIP, QueryDomain = Name;
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| extend NewProcImage = tolower(tostring(split(NewProcessName, "\\")[-1]))
| where NewProcImage in (SuspectClients)
   or NewProcessName has_any (@"\Users\Public\", @"\AppData\Local\Temp\", @"\AppData\Roaming\Microsoft\", @"\ProgramData\")
| where Account !endswith "$"
| join kind=inner (dnshits) on Computer
| where DnsTime between (TimeGenerated - 5m .. TimeGenerated + 5m)
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine, ParentProcessName,
          DnsTime, QueryDomain
| order by TimeGenerated desc
ucs.datadog_query: source:windows.sysmon @EventID:22 @QueryName:(*telegra.ph* OR *te.legra.ph* OR *graph.org* OR *t.me OR *telegram.org OR *ipfs.io* OR *cloudflare-ipfs.com*) -@Image:(*\chrome.exe OR *\Chrome.exe OR *\msedge.exe OR *\firefox.exe OR *\Firefox.exe OR *\brave.exe OR *\Telegram.exe OR *\telegram.exe OR *\TelegramDesktop.exe OR *\Teams.exe OR *\slack.exe OR *\opera.exe) (@Image:(*\mshta.exe OR *\MSHTA.EXE OR *\powershell.exe OR *\PowerShell.exe OR *\pwsh.exe OR *\wscript.exe OR *\WScript.exe OR *\cscript.exe OR *\CScript.exe OR *\rundll32.exe OR *\RunDll32.exe OR *\regsvr32.exe OR *\RegSvr32.exe OR *\certutil.exe OR *\CertUtil.exe OR *\curl.exe OR *\bitsadmin.exe OR *\hh.exe OR *\cmd.exe OR *\CMD.exe) OR @Image:(*\Users\Public\* OR *\AppData\Local\Temp\* OR *\AppData\Roaming\Microsoft\* OR *\ProgramData\*))
ucs.falcon_logscale_query:
#event_simpleName=DnsRequest
| DomainName=/(telegra\.ph|te\.legra\.ph|graph\.org|^t\.me$|telegram\.org|ipfs\.io|cloudflare-ipfs\.com)$/i
| NOT ContextImageFileName=/\\(chrome|msedge|firefox|brave|iexplore|opera|telegram|TelegramDesktop|Teams|slack|discord)\.exe$/i
| ContextImageFileName=/\\(mshta|powershell|pwsh|wscript|cscript|rundll32|regsvr32|certutil|curl|bitsadmin|hh|cmd)\.exe$/i OR ContextImageFileName=/\\(Users\\Public|AppData\\Local\\Temp|AppData\\Roaming\\Microsoft|ProgramData)\\/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ContextImageFileName, DomainName], function=count(as=hits))
| hits >= 1
ucs.rationale: Gamaredon's Pterodo / GammaLoad / GammaSteel family has been documented by Symantec, ESET, Cisco Talos, Palo Alto Unit 42 and CERT-UA since at least 2019 as using Telegram, Telegraph (telegra.ph / graph.org) and IPFS as one-way dead-drop resolvers, where C2 IPs are encoded in public posts so the implant can rotate hourly to defeat blocking. ucs.title: [LLM] Gamaredon Outlook VBA persistence via VbaProject.OTM / NormalEmail.dotm write by non-Office process
ucs.description: Detects modification of Outlook's VBA persistence files (VbaProject.OTM on classic Outlook, NormalEmail.dotm on Microsoft 365 Outlook) by any process other than Outlook or Office C2R updaters. This is the signature persistence technique of Gamaredon's PteroPSLoad / PteroLogon / PteroODoor modules, which inject VBA macros so the implant re-launches and exfils mail every time the user opens Outlook.
ucs.splunk:
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) AS firstTime max(_time) AS lastTime FROM datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    WHERE (Filesystem.file_name="VbaProject.OTM" OR Filesystem.file_name="NormalEmail.dotm" OR Filesystem.file_name="Outlook.dotm" OR Filesystem.file_name="*.OTM")
      AND (Filesystem.file_path="*\\Microsoft\\Outlook\\*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*\\Outlook\\*")
      AND Filesystem.action IN ("created","modified","renamed")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("outlook.exe","OUTLOOK.EXE","OfficeClickToRun.exe","msiexec.exe","setup.exe","OfficeC2RClient.exe","msoia.exe","onenote.exe","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
    BY Filesystem.dest Filesystem.user Filesystem.process_name Filesystem.file_path Filesystem.file_name Filesystem.action
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| where NOT match(user, "\\$$")
| `security_content_ctime(firstTime)`
| `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
| table firstTime lastTime dest user process_name file_path file_name action count
ucs.kql:
let LookbackDays = 30d;
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where ActionType in~ ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileRenamed")
| where FolderPath has_any (@"\Microsoft\Outlook\", @"\Outlook\")
| where FileName in~ ("VbaProject.OTM","NormalEmail.dotm","Outlook.dotm")
   or FileName endswith ".OTM"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("outlook.exe","officeclicktorun.exe","msiexec.exe","setup.exe","officec2rclient.exe","msoia.exe","onenote.exe","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName,
          AccountName = InitiatingProcessAccountName,
          FolderPath, FileName, ActionType,
          InitiatingProcessFileName,
          InitiatingProcessFolderPath,
          InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          ParentProcess = InitiatingProcessParentFileName,
          InitiatingProcessSHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ucs.sentinel_kql:
let LookbackDays = 30d;
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventType in~ ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileRenamed")
| where TargetFilePath has_any (@"\Microsoft\Outlook\", @"\Outlook\")
| where TargetFileName in~ ("VbaProject.OTM","NormalEmail.dotm","Outlook.dotm")
   or TargetFileName endswith ".OTM"
| where ActingProcessName !in~ ("outlook.exe","officeclicktorun.exe","msiexec.exe","setup.exe","officec2rclient.exe","msoia.exe","onenote.exe","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname,
          ActorUsername,
          TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, EventType,
          ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine,
          TargetFileSHA256
| order by TimeGenerated desc
ucs.sigma_yaml:
title: Gamaredon Outlook VBA Persistence via VbaProject.OTM / NormalEmail.dotm Write
id: e5d1b8a2-1c2a-4d3e-9c2f-7b6a4f3e2d1a
status: experimental
description: Detects writes to Outlook VBA persistence files (VbaProject.OTM, NormalEmail.dotm, Outlook.dotm) by any non-Office process. This is the signature persistence technique of Gamaredon (Shuckworm / Aqua Blizzard / Primitive Bear) PteroPSLoad / PteroLogon / PteroODoor implants.
references:
  - https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0047/
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1137/001/
  - https://symantec-enterprise-blogs.security.com/threat-intelligence/shuckworm-ukraine-gamaredon-russia
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/05/21
tags:
  - attack.persistence
  - attack.t1137.001
  - attack.g0047
logsource:
  category: file_event
  product: windows
detection:
  selection_path:
    TargetFilename|contains:
      - '\Microsoft\Outlook\'
      - '\Outlook\'
  selection_name:
    TargetFilename|endswith:
      - '\VbaProject.OTM'
      - '\NormalEmail.dotm'
      - '\Outlook.dotm'
      - '.OTM'
  filter_office:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\outlook.exe'
      - '\OfficeClickToRun.exe'
      - '\msiexec.exe'
      - '\setup.exe'
      - '\OfficeC2RClient.exe'
      - '\msoia.exe'
      - '\onenote.exe'
      - '\winword.exe'
      - '\excel.exe'
      - '\powerpnt.exe'
  filter_machine:
    User|endswith: '$'
  condition: selection_path and selection_name and not filter_office and not filter_machine
falsepositives:
  - Approved Outlook VBA add-ins deployed by enterprise IT — allowlist by SHA256 of the writer image
level: high
ucs.datadog_query: source:windows.sysmon @EventID:11 @TargetFilename:(*\Microsoft\Outlook\* OR *\Outlook\*) @TargetFilename:(*\VbaProject.OTM OR *\vbaproject.otm OR *\NormalEmail.dotm OR *\normalemail.dotm OR *\Outlook.dotm OR *.OTM OR *.otm) -@Image:(*\outlook.exe OR *\OUTLOOK.EXE OR *\OfficeClickToRun.exe OR *\OFFICECLICKTORUN.EXE OR *\msiexec.exe OR *\MsiExec.exe OR *\setup.exe OR *\Setup.exe OR *\OfficeC2RClient.exe OR *\msoia.exe OR *\onenote.exe OR *\ONENOTE.EXE OR *\winword.exe OR *\WINWORD.EXE OR *\excel.exe OR *\EXCEL.EXE OR *\powerpnt.exe OR *\POWERPNT.EXE) -@User:*$
ucs.falcon_logscale_query:
#event_simpleName=FileWritten
| TargetFileName=/\\Outlook\\/i
| TargetFileName=/(VbaProject\.OTM|NormalEmail\.dotm|Outlook\.dotm|\.OTM)$/i
| NOT ContextImageFileName=/\\(outlook|OfficeClickToRun|msiexec|setup|OfficeC2RClient|msoia|onenote|winword|excel|powerpnt)\.exe$/i
| NOT UserName=/\$$/
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, ContextImageFileName, TargetFileName], function=count(as=hits))
ucs.rationale: Outlook VBA template hijack is documented by Symantec/Broadcom (Shuckworm reports 2022-2024), ESET, Palo Alto Unit 42 (Trident Ursa) and CERT-UA as a hallmark of Gamaredon — they use it both for persistence (PteroLogon re-runs at every Outlook launch) and for mail exfiltration (PteroODoor monitors the Sent Items / Inbox via the same VBA project).
